methodology.arrival_model: Poisson arrivals with exponential inter-arrival times
methodology.server_model: Finite parallel processing slots; requests wait in a queue when all slots are busy
methodology.latency_model: Illustrative region-to-region base latency plus random jitter, queue wait, processing and any applicable failover delay
methodology.regional_server_failure: The central Europe region is considered failed for the entire experiment. Distributed requests can fail over to another region when failover is enabled.
methodology.network_link_failure: An abstract request-level route outage probability and independent packet-loss probability are applied. No specific physical link or actual route convergence is simulated.
methodology.packet_delivery_ratio: Delivered modeled packets divided by sent modeled packets, expressed as a percentage
methodology.availability: Successfully delivered requests divided by all attempted requests, expressed as a percentage
methodology.recovery_metric: Mean configured failover delay for successfully delivered requests that switched to a backup region. This is a modeled delay, not measured time to restore a failed system.
limitations: All latency, capacity, jitter, loss and failover values are model assumptions.
Failures are applied as experiment-wide scenarios, not timed events.
The model does not implement real routing protocols or physical links.
Python simulation results are separate from Cisco Packet Tracer observations.
